AC-1002-10.description: Error-message prefix discipline on supersede: rcfError messages returned from `src/blueprint/supersede.js` MUST NOT prepend their own `blueprint supersede: ` prefix — the CLI edge already writes `[error] blueprint supersede: ` on every rcfError from the supersede verb. AC-1002-3.description: Conflict output leads with per-side headers (ADR title + one-sentence decision) and names four honest resolution paths with actual blueprint slugs filled in (Phase 3.5 reshape)
AC-1002-3.then: the output opens with `conflict on topic (<topic>)` and one line per side carrying `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` (or `<id> at <path>` when the tree did not carry the ADR body), a `refs:` footer with both ids + paths, and four honest resolutions numbered 1-4: adopt-incoming (`rcf define blueprint remove <existing-slug>`), keep-existing (do not add the incoming), supersede via a project-level ADR (`rcf define blueprint supersede <topic>`), and declare-on-add (`rcf define blueprint add <source> --resolve <topic>=project:<ADR-id>`) — all with the actual conflicting blueprint slugs already substituted, no `<slug>` placeholders

AC-1002-4.description: Non-global TACs, ADRs, REQs, USs and FBSes are namespaced and cannot conflict

AC-1002-5.description: The supersession record's two sides are the CONFLICT PAIR — one currently-applied blueprint's scope:global ADR on the topic PLUS one incoming (would-be-applied) blueprint's scope:global ADR on the same topic — and the `rcf define blueprint supersede` verb accepts the incoming blueprint as the second side. Operator ruling (w-2026-08-19-008 round 3): option 3 as printed in the reshaped conflict message MUST be executable EXACTLY as printed from the refused-add state, with zero prep. Mechanism (builder judgement against the chain): the reshaped conflict message names option 3 as `rcf define blueprint supersede <topic> --incoming <source>`, carrying the very same `<source>` argument the refused add was invoked with; `supersede` loads the incoming blueprint from `--incoming <source>`, finds its scope:global ADR on `<topic>`, stamps its id into the incoming blueprint's namespace, and uses `{slug, adrId}` for the incoming blueprint as the second side of `manifest.resolutions[].supersedes[]`. The scaffolded project ADR file lists both blueprint ADR ids (applied + incoming stamped) under `relatedAdrs[]`; after supersede returns, re-running `rcf define blueprint add <source>` succeeds because the detector honours the freshly-recorded resolution. `--incoming <source>` is required when applied count on the topic is < 2 and is silently accepted (informational) when applied count is already >= 2.
AC-1002-5.given: a fresh project with ZERO applied blueprints and the shipped SPA + REST blueprints on disk (both carry scope:global ADRs on camelCase topics `errorEnvelope` and `authModel`)
AC-1002-5.when: the operator runs the flow verbatim as printed: `rcf define blueprint add <spa>`; `rcf define blueprint add <rest>` (refused with the reshaped four-honest-paths message); then follows option 3 EXACTLY as printed: `rcf define blueprint supersede errorEnvelope --incoming <rest>` and `rcf define blueprint supersede authModel --incoming <rest>`; then re-runs `rcf define blueprint add <rest>`
AC-1002-5.then: each supersede exits 0, scaffolds a project ADR at `rcf/adrs/adr-NNN-<kebab-topic>.json` (topic string verbatim on `manifest.resolutions[].topic`; ADR id tail kebab-ified per ADR-010), and appends a `manifest.resolutions[]` record listing both blueprint ADR ids in `supersedes[]`; the subsequent `rcf define blueprint add <rest>` exits 0 (detector honours the resolution) and both blueprint ADR files co-reside on disk with the project supersedes-ADR alongside them

AC-1002-6.description: `rcf define blueprint add --reason <text>` attaches the operator's ruling text to every `manifest.resolutions[]` record minted on that add. Whitespace-only reasons are refused at the writer edge (schema does not enforce a minimum floor on the field itself; the writer's floor is emptiness, not length).
AC-1002-6.given: an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on one or more topics, resolved via one or more --resolve declarations
AC-1002-6.when: the operator adds `--reason "..."` alongside the --resolve flags
AC-1002-6.then: every newly-minted resolutions[] record carries the reason string verbatim; a whitespace-only --reason exits 2 with an error naming the topic and no record is written

AC-1002-7.description: Duplicate `--resolve` declarations for the same topic within a single `rcf define blueprint add` are deduped: the first declaration is kept, subsequent declarations on the same topic are dropped, and a `[warn]` line names each dropped topic on stderr. The add still exits 0 on success; the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record per topic.
AC-1002-7.given: an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on topic X
AC-1002-7.when: the operator passes `--resolve X=project:ADR-A --resolve X=project:ADR-B` on the same command
AC-1002-7.then: the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record on topic X with `resolvedByAdrId: ADR-A` (first-wins), and stderr carries a warn line naming X as a duplicate --resolve topic

AC-1002-8.description: Conflict enrichment is symmetric: the CLI's conflict report and `--json` output both carry `title` + one-sentence `decision` on BOTH sides of a globalAdrTopic conflict — the existing side read from the walker's tree, the incoming side read from the blueprint's ADR file on disk. Round-1 only enriched the existing side, which read asymmetrically against shipped blueprints.
AC-1002-8.given: an incoming blueprint that would collide with an applied blueprint on a scope:global ADR topic, both ADRs carrying a title and a decision
AC-1002-8.when: `rcf define blueprint add <source>` refuses with the reshaped message (with or without --json)
AC-1002-8.then: both `incoming` and `existing` sides render `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` in the terminal output, and `conflicts[].incoming` and `conflicts[].existing` both carry `title` and `decision` in the --json output

AC-1002-9.description: Chain-level decision (ADR-010): the blueprint conflict-topic vocabulary is a FREE LABEL — a lookup key used by the detector (exact-match between an incoming ADR's topic and each applied ADR's topic) and stored verbatim on `manifest.resolutions[].topic`. No character-class constraint beyond the manifest schema's `minLength: 1` plus a writer-edge whitespace-only refuse. The shipped SPA + REST blueprints declare their scope:global ADR topics in camelCase (authModel, errorEnvelope, clientRouting, theming, clientState, apiVersioning, logging) and that vocabulary is canonical. Kebab-ification is confined to the projection into the ADR-id slug tail (ADR grammar requires kebab), never at the vocabulary edge.

AC-1002-9.when: supersede and add --resolve run on any of those topics as printed
AC-1002-9.then: the writer accepts the topic verbatim; the manifest.resolutions[].topic value byte-matches the applied ADR's topic; the scaffolded project ADR id carries a kebab-cased tail derived from the topic (`authModel` -> `ADR-NNN-auth-model`); no rcfError references 'kebab slug' or 'valid kebab' on any non-whitespace topic string

AC-1401-1.description: The loader accepts optional top-level `providesRoles` (non-empty array of lower camelCase strings on the pattern `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`) and optional top-level `suggestedCompanions` (non-empty array of `{role, reason}` objects; `role` is a lower camelCase string; `reason` is a non-empty string with no em-dashes and no emojis). Both fields are independent (a blueprint may provide a role AND suggest another; a blueprint may declare neither). Existing shelf blueprints (application-spa v1.4.0 baseline, observability-essentials v2.0.0, etc.) that declare neither still load clean.
AC-1401-1.then: the LoadedBlueprint object carries both fields verbatim and returns no rcfError; a blueprint declaring neither loads clean

AC-1401-2.description: The loader refuses (rcfError kind `validation`, exit 2 at the CLI edge) each of: a `providesRoles` value that fails the lower camelCase pattern (message names the offending index and value); a `suggestedCompanions` entry with a non-string or empty `role`; a `suggestedCompanions` entry with a missing, empty, or whitespace-only `reason`; a `suggestedCompanions` entry whose `reason` contains an em-dash (U+2014) or an emoji.
AC-1401-2.given: four separate mis-authored blueprint.json fixtures, one per refusal shape
AC-1401-2.then: each returns an rcfError of kind `validation` with a message naming the offending field and (for arrays) the index

AC-1401-3.then: the loader returns an rcfError of kind `validation` with the paired-ADR message exactly as specified

AC-1402-2.description: `rcf define blueprint add <service-slug> --companion <role>=<slug>` (repeatable) accepts `<libraryPrefix>:<slug>` for a library provider or a bare kebab slug for a shelf provider, validates that the named provider blueprint's `providesRoles[]` contains the role, refuses with exit 2 (`--companion <role>=<slug>: blueprint '<slug>' does not declare providesRoles containing '<role>'.`) when it does not, and writes the accepted choices to `rcf/companions.json` under `roles.<role>.provider` with a `pinnedAt` ISO-8601 timestamp.

AC-1403-2.description: `rcf define blueprint companions set <role> <slug>` writes `rcf/companions.json` under `roles.<role>.provider` with `pinnedAt` ISO-8601 (or updates it if present); refuses exit 2 when `<slug>` names no blueprint or the named blueprint does not declare `providesRoles` containing `<role>`. `rcf define blueprint companions unset <role>` removes the `roles.<role>` entry (leaves the rest of the file intact); refuses exit 2 when no pin exists for `<role>`. Both sub-verbs honour `--json` (emit `{ok: true, role, provider, pinnedAt}` on success; `{ok: false, error: {...}}` on refusal).

AC-1404-1.description: For each role suggested by an applied service blueprint, the resolver walks the tier ladder in order: (1) any applied blueprint whose `providesRoles[]` contains the role wins immediately with origin `already applied`; (2) otherwise, any registered library blueprint (from `rcf/blueprint-libraries.json` + each library's `library.json:blueprints[]`) whose source `providesRoles[]` contains the role wins with origin `registered library '<prefix>'`; (3) otherwise, the single core-shelf blueprint whose `providesRoles[]` contains the role wins with origin `shelf fallback`; (4) otherwise the role is unresolved (origin `unresolved`, provider null). A pin in `rcf/companions.json` overrides steps (2) and (3) with origin `pinned via rcf/companions.json` when the pin names a known provider.
AC-1404-1.given: three fixture projects: (a) core-only; (b) one registered library providing logging + the core provider; (c) an already-applied library-side logging provider

AC-1404-1.then: (a) resolves logging to observability-logging with `shelf fallback`; (b) resolves logging to the library provider with `registered library '<prefix>'`; (c) resolves logging to the applied library provider with `already applied`

AC-1404-2.then: the exit code is 3 and stderr carries the refusal message with both library slugs and the three resolution paths verbatim

AC-15601-1.description: rcf feedback preview renders each pending entry as the title and body that would be filed on GitHub (using src/feedback/render.js templates from section 4.3 of the design), lists the destination repo and its declared visibility (public, private, or unresolved), and prints the redaction ledger as diff-style lines ("- before  + after") with the rule name. --json emits the same as a machine-readable object per entry. No network calls. The kv-secret rule (design section 5 rule 5) is driven by the shared SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant exported from src/feedback/redact.js (design amendment R3a) so the first-pass redactor, the residual safeguard pass and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner cover exactly the same open vocabulary of key stems (secret, token, password, passwd, passphrase, pw, pwd, pass, key, apikey/api_key/api-key, privatekey/private_key/private-key, accesskey/access_key/access-key, clientsecret/client_secret/client-secret, bearer, credential/credentials/cred/creds, session, cookie, signature, sig, salt; hash carries a 16+-value length guard); the match is right-bounded at a word edge so `keyword` and `authors` do not fold but `dbpassword` still does. Design amendment R4 (round 5) extends the rule-5 pass so a vocabulary key labelling a value-shape token of 8+ chars with any separator (markdown table pipes, whitespace runs, tabs, hyphens, arrows, HTML numeric entities, or the prose bridges is / was / set to) also folds, with a mixed-classes gate on the value that keeps ordinary prose (`the password is required`, `the password field is required`) intact.

AC-15601-4.description: After rendering and normalising the fully assembled issue body (and, for the bundle path, each bundle file), a final whole-text residual-secret pass runs findResidualSecrets over the whole text with multiline patterns. Any hit means the entry stays pending (preview marks it refused-residual and submit refuses that entry with exit 3) and no create/comment/bundle-write occurs for it. The safeguard is defence-in-depth: it catches multiline shapes (e.g. an em-dash-delimited PEM block that survives per-field redaction of a slice-2-style body) that a per-line scan could not see. The safeguard shares the SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant with the first-pass redactor and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner (design amendment R3a), so a shortname-key value (`pw=...`, `pwd=...`) or a webhook-path shape (`/services/<token>`, `/api/webhooks/<token>`, `/bot<token>/method`) that reappears after per-field normalisation is caught by the same set the first pass used.

AC-15601-4.then: preview surfaces the residual line and the tainted entry stays pending; submit exits 3 without a create/comment for that entry and without writing a bundle whose text carries the residual shape

AC-15601-5.description: The operator-identity substitution (design section 5 rule 6) applies word-boundary and stopword guards so a common noun that happens to appear in the operator's identity name is not folded. A RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS constant, exported from src/feedback/redact.js and defence-in-depth applied at every operator-name token loop, blocks the fold when the whitespace-separated token (case-insensitive) is one of: agent, agents, user, users, operator, operators, admin, admins, root, client, clients, server, servers, service, services, system, systems, name, main, test, code, api, apis, anon, anonymous, human, humans, dev, ops, sre, docs, developer, developers, engineer, engineers, team, teams. Substitution still fires for a real given name (Alice, Smith) even when the full identity string contains a stopword. The URL and prose canon phrase 'the agent files feedback' survives unmodified when the identity contains 'agent'. Rationale: the rcf-lite ecosystem uses 'agent' as a canonical noun (RULE 17, docs paths); operator-identity folds must be driven by real identity values, never by a bare common noun.

AC-15601-6.description: The rule-4 bare-hostname redactor treats filename tokens carrying a known file extension as NOT hostnames. A candidate hostname match whose trailing dot-label is in a bundled FILE_EXTENSIONS set (initially md, mdx, json, yml, yaml, txt, js, mjs, cjs, ts, tsx, html, css, png, svg, sh, csv, log, lock) is left intact and no ledger row is written for it (design amendment R5d). The negative lookbehind on the hostname regex additionally excludes '-' so that filename fragments embedded in a larger identifier (`Backstory-product-brief.md`) cannot start a match after a hyphen. The extension shortlist is merged at call time from an `extensions` array on src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json alongside the existing `hosts` field, so operators can extend it the same way they extend hosts. Design amendment R5e (added 0.28.3 per HQ 2026-09-22 ruling on Codex P1-5 deferred from PR #242): candidate hostnames whose trailing dot-label is a single letter are also treated as filename fragments, not hostnames. Rationale: single-letter TLDs are not registrable domains in normal prose and folding them yields more false positives (short identifiers, abbreviated references) than legitimate hostname redactions. Design amendment R5f (added 0.28.3, #243): the rule-3 email regex is bounded so it does not consume the git protocol sentinel `git@<host>` inside a URL whose scheme is `git+ssh://`, `ssh://` or `git://`, nor the bare git-remote shape `git@<host>:<owner>/<repo>` (colon followed by a non-space path). Rationale: `git@<host>` is a URI userinfo construct, not an email; folding it destroys evidence pointers copied from git remotes and clone URLs. Real email addresses in surrounding prose still fold. Design amendment R5g (added 0.28.3, #246): when the operator identity Name (rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name) is empty, whitespace only, or contains only reserved-noun tokens (RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS from AC-15601-5), buildRedactionContext emits a one-line visible warning to stderr naming the file and stating that identity folding is disabled. The warning is emitted once per redaction context build. Folding still skips (per AC-15601-5) but the operator is no longer left thinking their identity is in force.
AC-15601-6.given: a fixture project with a body containing the tokens 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json', 'report.log', 'foo.example.com', 'foo.example.com/path', 'Backstory-example.com', 'a.b.c', the URL 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0', the URL 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git', the bare git remote 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git', and a prose email 'alice@example.com'; and a rcf/.identity/profile.md whose ## Name line is either absent, whitespace only, or reads 'The Agent Operator' (stopword-only)
AC-15601-6.when: the redactor runs over the body with the default allowlist
AC-15601-6.then: 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json' and 'report.log' survive verbatim with no ledger row for a hostname substitution on their basename; 'foo.example.com' folds to <host> via rule 4; 'foo.example.com/path' folds via rule 4 bare-host (the URL rule requires a scheme; the token here has none); 'Backstory-example.com' folds to '<host>' (the trailing label is not in the extension set); 'a.b.c' survives verbatim with no hostname ledger row (single-letter trailing label per R5e); 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0' survives verbatim - the `git@` sentinel is NOT rewritten by the email rule (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist; 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f stash) and the host `example.internal` folded to '<host>' by the extended URL rule 4 which now matches ssh/git+ssh/git schemes with optional userinfo; 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist so it survives verbatim; 'alice@example.com' in surrounding prose still folds to '<email>' (rule 3 email); and when the identity Name is empty/whitespace/stopword-only, stderr carries exactly one visible warning line naming rcf/.identity/profile.md and stating that identity folding is disabled. Extending the allowlist with `extensions: ["xyz"]` in redact-allowlist.json (or the operator overlay) makes 'file.xyz' also survive.

AC-15701-1.description: fingerprint(entry) returns the first 12 hex chars of sha-256 over "<kind>|<targetKey>|<anchor>|<symptomClass>" where targetKey is the effective slug for blueprints (no version) or the verb path for core, anchor is upper-cased or "-" when absent, and symptomClass is one of the closed enum. AC-15701-2.description: On submit, per pending entry, gh search issues is called for the destination repo with query "rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp>", --match body, --state open, --limit 5. For every returned candidate, submit re-reads the candidate issue body via gh issue view --json body (ghIssueGetBody) and folds ONLY if the body contains a line exactly matching "rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp>" on its own; a search hit whose body does not carry that exact line is a NON-MATCH and is discarded. Anchor and target must also match the entry's anchor and target; folding across a differing anchor or target is refused even when the fingerprint lines are equal. Zero verified hits: gh issue create; the stdout row reports "created #N (<title>)". One or more verified hits: gh issue comment on the lowest-numbered verified issue, mention any other verified hits in the comment body, and post the FULL rendered report (title as a "## Report" heading, then the redacted body, then evidence and environment tables, then the fingerprint line), labelled as "Apparent duplicate of the issue subject; posting the full report so a human can judge." The retired "+1 from another reporter." payload is never posted. The stdout row on the fold path reports "commented on #N (fingerprint match: <title>)" so a wrong match is visible on the same line a human already sees.
AC-15701-2.given: a fake gh module (via RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE) whose ghIssueSearch stub yields zero, one and two hits in three sequential invocations, and one pending entry per case; and a second fixture where ghIssueSearch returns a candidate whose ghIssueGetBody body carries a DIFFERENT fingerprint line to the entry; and a third fixture where the candidate body's fingerprint matches but the candidate's anchor or target field differs from the entry's
AC-15701-2.when: rcf feedback submit --yes runs against each fixture
AC-15701-2.then: the zero-hit case creates and prints "created #N (<title>)"; the one-hit case with a verified fingerprint match comments on the returned number, the comment body carries the full rendered report (title + body + evidence + environment + fingerprint), the string "+1 from another reporter." is absent, and the stdout row prints "commented on #N (fingerprint match: <title>)"; the two-hit case comments on the smaller number and mentions the other verified number; the different-fingerprint fixture and the differing-anchor/target fixture both fall through to create rather than comment

AC-1601-1.description: `rcf audit eval coverage --strict` exits 0 on a chain with zero nonDeterministic ACs and exits 4 on any nonDeterministic AC without a resolving EVAL (a non-superseded EVAL whose most recent runRecord entry is not pending). Non-strict runs always exit 0; the mermaid format colours the AC glyph green (deterministic), amber (covered) or red (missing).

AC-1601-2.description: The verify verdict layer emits EVAL-MISSING on any nonDeterministic AC without a resolving EVAL and EVAL-BELOW-THRESHOLD on any nonDeterministic AC whose bound EVAL last ran with verdict fail. Deterministic ACs never emit either verdict. Both entries ride report.perAcVerdicts[] without expanding the top-level VERDICTS set (backward compatibility on validateReportShape). runStats.evalCoverage rolls up the counts and the CLI prints the preflight line on stderr.

AC-1601-3.description: rcf finalise refuses (exit 4) with the spec-verbatim message when the verify report carries EVAL-MISSING or EVAL-BELOW-THRESHOLD, and accepts --ship-without-eval <reason> (mandatory reason string; exit 2 without one, refused when the value looks like a flag). The acknowledgement lands on the manifest under shipWithoutEval[] with a monotonic id, the reason, the declared per-AC verdicts and the report path.

AC-1601-4.description: The LLM-as-judge run path spawns claude (or codex) on PATH, passes the per-case payload on stdin, captures stdout, validates against the declared response schema and composes a runRecord[] entry (aggregateScore, criticalFailures, verdict). No API keys or HTTP APIs enter rcf-lite; the estate subscription-only rule holds. The grader's aggregate verdict is a non-deterministic judgement over graded output, which is the correct home for an EVAL contract on the dogfood tree.

AC-16101-1.description: The quiet rule in src/feedback/hook.js returns "ask" on stop when ALL hold: not opted out (rcf/feedback-settings.json ask true and RCF_FEEDBACK_ASK unset or 1); at least one pending entry; state.json has no asked record for the incoming session_id; stop_hook_active is false; and one of: an entry carries askNow; the newest pending entry is older than quietMinutes (default 15) minutes; the queue-state cache reports complete or nothing actionable; the entry was carried over. AC-16101-2.description: On Claude Code (--harness claude-code default when CLAUDECODE is set), the stop hook exits 2 with the reason text on stderr. On Codex (--harness codex), the hook emits stdout JSON { "decision": "block", "reason": "<same text>" } with exit 0. Both branches append the asked record to state.json exactly once per session_id. AC-16101-3.description: A second stop invocation with the same session_id is silent (no exit-2, no JSON block emission, exit 0) even when new pending entries arrive after the first ask. A new session_id resets the ledger and asks again per the quiet rule.

Two bundles it writes in the same second for different pending sets are both kept: neither overwrites the other, and each one's bytes are in exactly one file of the outbox.

AC-16103-2.description: rcf feedback hook session-start with pending entries and a new sessionId prints one plain line to stdout on Claude Code ("rcf feedback: <n> unsubmitted entr(y|ies) carried over from an earlier session; ask the operator once at a natural pause (RULE 17).") and the Codex-shaped equivalent under --harness codex. The line is what the harness injects as context; it never blocks. If SessionStart on Codex cannot inject context (verified at build time against the current Codex reference), the fallback in RULE 17 ("check rcf feedback status at session start") is what carries the same posture.

AC-16103-3.description: rcf feedback defer means "not now, ask again next session" (design 3.1). Entries in status deferredUntilSession whose stored sessionId is not the current one are requeued to pending on the SessionStart hook AND on the Stop hook (belt to the SessionStart braces, so the flow works when only Stop is installed). The requeue appends one state-transition line per entry with status pending and no sessionId field, so fold-by-id preserves the entry's prior sessionId and the carry-over gate in both hooks (pending.sessionId !== currentSessionId) fires naturally in the new session. Entries recorded or last deferred under the current sessionId are not re-transitioned (idempotent per session; deferring twice in one session is a no-op on the second call).
AC-16103-3.given: a fixture with one pending entry deferred in session A (entries.jsonl carries the deferredUntilSession line with sessionId A)
AC-16103-3.when: rcf feedback hook session-start --harness claude-code is run with session_id B, then rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code is run with the same session_id B
AC-16103-3.then: SessionStart appends one { status: pending } transition (no sessionId field) so the entry returns to pending with its sessionId still A; the carry-over line prints to stdout naming the count and RULE 17; the following Stop exits 2 with the ask on stderr and appends exactly one asked record for session B; a second SessionStart in session B is a no-op (no new transition, silent stdout); a further SessionStart in a fresh session_id C after a Stop-only path (no SessionStart wired) still requeues on the Stop hook so the ask fires there

AC-16103-4.description: [must-not] A feedback entry recorded in a linked git worktree is never lost with the worktree and never left where the main checkout would commit it. The queue of a linked worktree lives in the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/ (the round 1 storage choice). An entry rcf feedback add records in a linked worktree is offered from the main checkout after git worktree remove. A queue the worktree already holds in its own .rcf/feedback/ (as 0.36.0 left it) is moved into the main checkout's store by the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree (any sub-verb, the Stop, SessionEnd and SessionStart hooks included) once the main checkout's .gitignore covers .rcf/feedback/, so no entry, old or new, is lost when the worktree is removed, and each keeps its id (listed once) and its status. While the main checkout does not ignore .rcf/feedback/, nothing moves: rcf feedback list and the hooks in that worktree keep reading its own held queue (the Stop hook keeps asking about its pending entries), and rcf feedback add there without --force exits 2, stderr naming .rcf/feedback, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory and saying "the held entries move into the main checkout once it ignores .rcf/feedback/", and writes nothing under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/; once the main checkout ignores the store, the next rcf feedback command in the worktree moves the held queue as above. If the move fails (for example the main checkout's .rcf/ or a file the move writes there is not writable, or a held file cannot be removed from the worktree), the command exits 1 with stderr naming the error the move hit and the main checkout's directory, and nothing is written to the worktree's queue; the failed move loses nothing and duplicates nothing: every entry the worktree held stays readable from the worktree or the main checkout, a held file is removed only after its content is present in the main store, and the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree, once what made the move fail is put right, completes the move with each id once. Commands that run at the same time change none of this: when two or more rcf feedback commands run in the worktree at once (or in two linked worktrees of one main checkout, each moving its own held queue), or rcf feedback add, a hook or rcf feedback submit writes to the main checkout's store while the move runs, each entry line, ask record and outbox bundle the worktree held lands in the main checkout's store exactly once (never duplicated, overwritten or lost), and an entry or outbox bundle written while the move runs is kept (a bundle in exactly one file of the main checkout's outbox). The main checkout's own ask records are kept the same way: every ask record the main checkout's state.json held before the move, and every ask record its Stop hook writes while the move runs, is in it exactly once afterwards, and a command that reads the main checkout's state.json while another command writes it reads a whole document (a Stop hook in a session that already asked stays silent). A command that reads the main checkout's entries.jsonl while another command writes it (rcf feedback add recording an entry, or a command recording an entry's new status) reads only whole lines, never a partial one. A command that writes to the main checkout's store (rcf feedback add, the Stop hook, the SessionEnd hook or rcf feedback submit) while a move is still changing that store waits for the move for up to 10 seconds; if the move is still running then, the writer exits 1 with stderr naming the running command's process id and the main checkout's directory, and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/. A move whose process stopped without finishing (no longer running on this host), or that has not been refreshed for 60 seconds, holds up no later command: the next command proceeds, and the next rcf feedback command run in the worktree completes the move with each id once. A move still running is refreshed at least every 5 seconds while it works, so it is never taken for stopped however long ago it started: a writer waiting on it exits 1 as above once its wait runs out. When two or more commands find the same stopped move at once, exactly one of them goes on at any instant: every other writer waits as above and every other move leaves its held queue for a later command, no command sets aside a command still running or one that went on after the stopped move, and each entry line, ask record and outbox bundle any of them writes is in the main checkout's store exactly once. A command that holds the main checkout's store and is judged stopped by a later command while it still runs (it was held up for more than 60 seconds, or its clock is behind the later command's) writes nothing more to the main checkout's store once the later command has taken the store over: it exits 1 with stderr naming the path of the record of its hold that it lost, and every write the later command made is kept. A command that stopped (no longer running on this host) while it was taking over a stopped move holds up no later command either, and the command that goes on past it removes the claim it left in the main checkout's store. A command's record in the main checkout's store that cannot be read (its file cannot be parsed) is judged by that file's age: it holds up no later command once the file is more than 60 seconds old, and a writer it holds up past its wait exits 1 and writes nothing under the main checkout's .rcf/feedback/, with stderr naming that file's path and its age in seconds. The write with which rcf feedback submit records an issue or comment it has already filed is never abandoned on a busy store: it waits for up to 65 seconds by its clock, so a move that stopped refreshing is judged stopped within it and the record lands; if it still cannot write then, submit exits 1 with stderr naming the filed issue's URL and the entry's id, never saying it wrote nothing, and the next rcf feedback submit does not file that entry again. This holds in a linked worktree too: a filing that rcf feedback submit run in the worktree could not record while the worktree kept its own held queue (the main checkout's .gitignore did not cover .rcf/feedback/ yet) moves into the main checkout's store with that queue, exactly once, so the next rcf feedback submit in either checkout does not file that entry again and no held file is left under the worktree's .rcf/feedback/. Whenever rcf feedback submit has already filed or recorded anything (an issue or comment it filed, or a filing an earlier submit kept that it recorded) and a later write of the same run finds the main checkout's store busy past its wait, it exits 1 with stderr naming each entry it filed or recorded by its id and the issue's URL, never saying it wrote nothing. rcf feedback submit --dry-run writes nothing and never lists an entry whose filing an earlier submit kept (filed, not yet recorded) among the entries it would file, comment on or bundle. A Stop hook that does not ask (the operator opted out) and has nothing to write never waits: it exits at once as it would alone. The gitignore pre-write check of rcf feedback add runs against the checkout that holds the store: when the main checkout's .gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/, rcf feedback add in the worktree without --force refuses as AC-15501-2 refuses (exit 2, stderr names the missing .rcf/feedback/ entry, rcf doctor --fix and the main checkout's directory) and nothing is created under either checkout's .rcf/feedback/. When the main checkout does not hold the rcf project (rcf adopted on the worktree's branch only), rcf feedback add in the worktree never leaves a file the main checkout would commit; keeping the entry in the worktree or refusing is the builder's choice, and that worktree's queue surviving its removal is out of scope. Worktrees of a bare repository and separate-git-dir worktrees are out of scope. AC-15501-1 and AC-15501-2 are unchanged.

AC-16104-1.description: rcf init merges three feedback hook entries into .claude/settings.json (Stop -> "npx rcf-lite feedback hook stop --harness claude-code" timeout 10; SessionEnd -> "... hook session-end ..." timeout 5; SessionStart matcher "startup|resume" -> "... hook session-start ...") and three matching entries into .codex/hooks.json (in the Codex schema for the same events). Merge discipline mirrors writeMcpConfig: parse, refuse on invalid JSON with the same message shape as .mcp.json, never clobber other hooks, add ours only if an entry whose command contains "rcf feedback hook" is absent. The "npx rcf-lite" prefix is replaced by binPath when init was called with --bin-path, mirroring the .mcp.json entry pattern.
AC-16104-1.given: a fresh fixture project with no .claude/settings.json and no .codex/hooks.json
AC-16104-1.then: both files contain the three feedback hook entries in the right shape; a second rcf init on the same tree is byte-idempotent; a pre-existing settings.json with an unrelated hook is preserved and the feedback entries are added alongside it

AC-16104-2.description: rcf init --no-feedback-hooks writes neither .claude/settings.json nor .codex/hooks.json feedback entries and prints the instruction-only fallback line once (RULE 17 still applies). --no-feedback-hooks composes with --no-playwright-mcp and other init skips without interaction.
AC-16104-2.then: no feedback hook entry is present in either config file; init exits 0; the one-line instruction fallback appears in stdout

AC-16104-3.description: rcf doctor --check feedback-hooks reports missing-hook (fixable) per hook per file when an expected entry is absent, and foreign-hook (refused, hand-repair message) when an entry whose command contains "rcf feedback hook" is present with different flags than the current install shape. rcf doctor --fix adds the missing entries and touches nothing else. A clean tree reports no findings and doctor stays exit 0.
AC-16104-3.given: three fixture projects: one missing all feedback hook entries; one with a foreign entry (same command, wrong flags); one clean
AC-16104-3.when: rcf doctor --check feedback-hooks --fix is run against each
AC-16104-3.then: the missing-entries project ends with the entries present (added only); the foreign-entry project keeps the foreign entry, reports the foreign-hook message and exits non-zero; the clean project makes no writes and exits 0

AC-17001-1.description: The rendered review-surface HTML carries a "product-map" tab (data-tab="product-map") in tab order after Build sequence, with a hidden tabpanel id "tab-product-map" containing a shape-grouping section whose bucket headings enumerate every shape the classified REQs use plus "Unclassified" and "Business rules". A REQ classified into two shapes appears in both buckets. Rendering does not require a schema change.

AC-17001-2.description: Selecting the shape grouping drills each bucket to its REQs (rendered with the same doc-details helper and status pill as the Requirements tab), each REQ to its user stories, and each user story to its acceptance criteria, so the reader can go from a shape bucket to an AC in the same tab. Grouping button clicks and status filter changes push a new history entry (Back/Forward traverse them); top-level tab clicks keep their existing behaviour.

AC-17002-1.description: The Product Map tab carries a status filter control whose options are the five authoring statuses plus "all", and applies to every grouping on the tab. When "approved" is selected the tab renders only REQs whose status is approved. Buckets that become empty under the current filter are hidden by default with a summary line ("N empty" - clicking reveals them), so the map keeps its shape without rendering a wall of empty headings.

AC-17003-1.description: When the Product Map is grouped by component, the tab renders the TAD as the root, one section per TAC (with a short dependencies[] list drawn from the TAC document), then the user stories under that TAC (from usByTacId), then their parent REQs (from us.reqId), then the ACs. REQs reachable by no TAC are collected under an "Unmapped" bucket with a count in its heading.

AC-17004-1.description: The trace-coverage grouping buckets each REQ into one of complete | missing-stories | missing-ac-scope | missing-component | missing-tests, computed from the tree-model maps (storiesByReqId, acIdsByUsId, usByTacId, tsByAcId / tcsByAcId / fbsByAcId). Each REQ row states in plain text exactly what is missing, and links to its own doc anchor so the reader can jump to it.

AC-17005-1.description: The capability grouping enumerates one bucket per distinct capability:<slug> value present on any REQ across the tree. A REQ carrying multiple capability tags appears under each. REQs whose tags carry no capability:<slug> entry are collected under an "Unclassified" bucket. Slugs are rendered as their kebab form in the heading; named capability buckets are ordered by REQ count desc, then alphabetically, and the Unclassified bucket is always pinned last.

AC-17006-1.description: The Product Map tab renders every bucket collapsed by default, with a summary row carrying the bucket label, its total REQ count and a mini count per authoring status (draft / review / needsRevision / approved / superseded). A jump-nav rail across the top of the panel lists every bucket in the active grouping with its count; clicking a chip scrolls to that bucket and opens it. The hash schema `#tab=product-map&group=<g>&status=<s>&open=<id1>,<id2>` restores tab, grouping, status filter AND the set of open buckets on return, and every bucket-toggle pushes a new history entry so Back/Forward traverse them. Per-bucket <details> nodes carry a stable data-doc-id ("pm-bucket:<group>:<id>") so the live-client persists their open state across SSE refreshes.

AC-17007-1.description: The Product Map first-load payload target is well under 3 MB. The server emits the shape (default) grouping fully; the other three groupings emit only their bucket headings (label + total count + per-status mini counts) and each bucket carries a data-pm-lazy marker naming its grouping and bucket id. When the reader switches to a lazy grouping OR opens a lazy bucket, the client fetches that grouping fully once (from a partial endpoint the server exposes) and hydrates the bucket into the DOM; subsequent switches use the cached partial. The pass doc states the before/after first-load bytes.

AC-17008-1.description: Every REQ row inside the Product Map tab that was contributed by an applied blueprint carries a compact blueprint badge (class pm-blueprint-badge) in its summary row, in every grouping (shape, component, trace coverage, capability, and the new by-blueprint grouping itself). The GROUPINGS list on the panel additionally includes 'blueprint'; the by-blueprint grouping enumerates one bucket per entry in manifest.blueprints[] (label: the blueprint's display name or slug, count: number of contributed REQs) plus an Application bucket for the project's own (non-blueprint) REQs (REQs with no blueprint attribution). Inside each blueprint or Application bucket, requirements are split by capability (existing capability:<slug> convention) as a second level, then the usual REQ->US->AC drill-down. The source of truth for blueprint attribution is manifest.blueprints[].contributions[] (parsed by scope.contributionsForBlueprint); the id-prefix fallback (kebab-slug prefix on reqId) is used only when the manifest carries no contributions record for a given blueprint. The hash schema round-trips as #tab=product-map&group=blueprint&status=<s>&open=<ids>, and the /product-map/blueprint partial endpoint serves the grouping body for the client's lazy-render fetch. A project with no applied blueprints renders a single Application bucket cleanly (not an error, not an empty tab).

AC-1701-1.description: The pack loader discovers `.pack.js` and `.pack.mjs` modules under `blueprints/<slug>/probe-packs/` for every applied blueprint, imports each with a dynamic ESM import, validates the exported default object against the pack schema (`packName` starts with the owning blueprint's slug and matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, `version` semver, `blueprintSlug` matches the directory, `checks[]` non-empty with each entry carrying `id`, `severity` in {block, warn, advisory}, `description` and async `run`), and refuses at load (exit 2) with a diagnostic that names the pack path and the offending field on any violation. A valid pack registers on the run.

AC-1701-2.description: The applicability predicate `appliesTo({ fbs, uiBaseline, manifest })` is a required top-level field on every pack; its source (`appliesTo.toString()`) MUST reference at least one of `route`, `tacIds`, or the `blueprint:` US-tag prefix, and an unqualified predicate (a body that references none of the three, including the default `() => true`) is refused at load with exit 2 and a diagnostic that names the pack, the requirement and the three legal scoping seams. A pack whose `appliesTo` returns `false` for an FBS records `applicable: false` on the record for that FBS with a one-line reason drawn from the predicate context and no `run` function is invoked.

AC-1701-3.description: The loader cross-checks every `checks[].id` against the AC ids the pack's blueprint contributes through `blueprint.json:contributions[]` (reading each US contribution file and enumerating `acceptanceCriteria[].id`). A pack whose check names an AC id the blueprint does not contribute is refused at load (exit 2) with a diagnostic that names the pack, the offending check id and the AC ids the blueprint actually contributes.

AC-1701-4.description: The runner runs the pack pass after invariants and after auth-smoke on `agentScreenshotCritique` mode. For each applicable pack the runner invokes every check's `run({ browser, fetch, runtimeUrl, route, theme })` (browser and fetch injected by the runner), records `{ id, verdict, severity, detail? }` on the pack record, and appends the pack record to `browserVerification.probePacks[]` on the composed record. The aggregate verdict extends the existing rule: `block` on any pack check whose severity is `block` and verdict is `fail`; `warn` on any pack check whose severity is `warn` and verdict is `fail` (and no block from invariants, auth-smoke or pack); `pass` otherwise.

AC-1701-5.description: `rcf verify browser <fbs-id> --probe-pack <name>` restricts one run to one pack by name; a `--probe-pack` value that resolves to no discovered pack (nothing loaded under any applied blueprint's `probe-packs/` matches the name) exits 2 with a diagnostic that names the value and the packs that were discovered. When omitted, every discovered and applicable pack runs; when a pack's `appliesTo` returns false for the FBS, the pack record carries `applicable: false` and no browser check runs against it.

AC-1701-6.description: A pack MAY declare `preChecks[]`: an array of `{ id, description, run: async () => ({ verdict, detail? }) }` Node build-scan fast-fail checks that the runner invokes before any browser check on the same pack. A pre-check with verdict `fail` records on the pack record and every browser check that names it under `dependsOn` records verdict `skipped` with detail `skipped-by-pre-check:<preCheckId>`; browser checks with no `dependsOn` on a failing pre-check still run. Pre-check verdicts fold into the aggregate the same way pack checks do (a `fail` at `severity: block` blocks ship).

AC-1701-7.description: The `packBrowser` seam the runner injects into every pack check is a real headless browser provisioned through the pinned Playwright MCP server (`PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION` in `src/verify/engine/launcher.js`, spawned as `npx -y @playwright/mcp@<pin>` over stdio) via a thin in-package JSON-RPC 2.0 client (zero new npm dependencies in rcf-lite; no LLM call). Every check receives a stable API: `goto(url)`, `snapshot()` returning accessibility-tree text, `evaluate(fn, arg?)` returning a parsed value, `click(selector, hint?)`, `type(selector, text, hint?)`, `press(key)`, `screenshot(filename?)`, `close()`. When the consuming project already resolves `playwright` from its own `node_modules`, the runner MAY take that cheaper direct route and expose the identical API; the pinned MCP version remains the source of the browser otherwise. The CLI provisions the browser only when at least one applicable pack is loaded and `--no-browser` was not passed; `deps.packBrowser` on the CLI handler overrides the provisioning for tests.

AC-1701-8.description: A pack MAY declare a `boot: { bootCommand, waitForUrl, waitForSelector }` object. Before running the pack pass, the CLI probes the runtime URL; when it responds with any HTTP status the boot is skipped and the running server is used unchanged. When the runtime is not answering AND `boot.bootCommand` is a non-empty string, the CLI spawns `bootCommand` from the project root (Node.js child_process, cwd=projectRoot, no shell), polls `waitForUrl` at a bounded interval until a timeout, and when the URL responds runs the packs; when `waitForSelector` is set and a browser is available, the CLI navigates the browser to `waitForUrl` and polls the accessibility snapshot for a substring match on the selector until a bounded timeout (soft-failure only, packs still run). The CLI stops any process it started in reverse order after the pack pass completes (SIGTERM then SIGKILL fallback after 3s). `--no-boot` disables the fallback and forces packs to run against whatever the runtime URL currently answers. When the runtime is unreachable AND no `bootCommand` is declared, the CLI records the note and proceeds; the pack's own runtime checks then surface the failure.

AC-17101-1.description: Every REQ under packages/rcf-lite/rcf/requirements/ carries at least one tag matching the regex ^capability:[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, and every slug used maps to an entry in the documented capability taxonomy.

AC-17102-1.description: packages/rcf-lite/docs contains a capability tags section listing every slug in the initial taxonomy with a one-line meaning, plus the rule for adding a new capability (single-word verb or noun, kebab-case, must map to a product surface). The section is linked from docs/README.md so it is reachable from the docs entry point.

AC-17201-1.description: computeDelta(tree, freeze, ledgers) returns the exact object shape proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 2.2 specifies (frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, changed, added, removed, briefSince, unchanged); given a matching freeze the delta reports empty changed / added / removed and unchanged equal to the number of docHashes; given divergent tree state changed / added / removed classify every id correctly against the freeze record.

AC-17201-2.description: hashDocument returns a sha256:<64-hex> string over the canonical JSON form of the parsed document (keys sorted recursively, no whitespace), and is invariant under a whitespace-only reformat or a key reorder: two documents that parse to the same object hash identically.

AC-17201-3.description: Loading rcf/define/freeze.json when the file is absent returns null; loading a malformed file (bad JSON, missing docHashes, non-sha256 hash value, negative briefStatements) raises FreezeRecordError with a code (parseFailure or schemaFailure) and a named field so a caller can log the exact failure.

AC-17201-4.description: Saving then loading a freeze record round-trips every documented field including extension fields the schema does not police (counts, litmus, versions, note), and saveFreezeRecord refuses to persist an invalid record: no file is written on validation failure.

AC-17301-1.description: rcf define ledger brief add --kind <k> --text <t> appends a numbered statement to rcf/define/brief-ledger.json, mints the next id (highest current + 1), stamps status open and addedAt (ISO-8601), refuses an unknown kind with a usage-class error, and refuses --text combined with --from with a usage-class error.

AC-17301-2.description: rcf define ledger decisions list prints the numbered #241 format: one decision per item (id. question), options rendered as 'letter) text', the default letter labelled 'default:', and what it blocks labelled 'blocks:'. rcf define ledger <name> list --json emits the machine-readable envelope { ledger, <arrayKey>: [...] }.

AC-17301-3.description: rcf define ledger brief add --from <file> reads the file, splits it into one statement per non-empty line (stripping leading '- ', '* ' or '<n>. ' bullets), mints sequential ids for every statement, refuses if the file produced zero non-empty lines, and stamps the file path as source unless --source overrides it. The intake-scan-against-frozen-statements hook is a named seam in the writer, not called in this slice.

AC-17301-4.description: walkTree run over a project that carries rcf/define/freeze.json, all four ledger files, and a bug-bait file named req-999.json under rcf/define/ never surfaces any rcf/define/ file as a tree.byId document and reports no walker error naming a rcf/define/ path. The sidecar directory is invisible to every consumer of walkTree.

AC-17302-1.description: [happy] given statement 7, when rcf define ledger brief update 7 --kind constraint --resolved-by REQ-003 runs, then the statement carries kind constraint and resolvedBy REQ-003 and its id and addedAt are unchanged.

AC-17302-10.description: [happy] (R1 create extension 2026-10-05, PR 292 follow-up; amended on the PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create ac --parent US-1 --id AC-1-1 --description "foo" on a tree where US-1 already carries AC-1-1 with description foo and testable true and no other fields, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'AC-1-1: unchanged (rcf/user-stories/us-1.json)'; the parent US file is not rewritten; and given the same verb with --description "bar" instead, it exits 3, stderr names the id and the differing field (description), and the file is not rewritten. rcf define create has no --json flag; the stdout line is the whole output (suppressed by --quiet).

AC-17302-11.description: [happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create tc --parent TS-1 --id TC-1-foo --ac AC-1-1 --description "foo" --test-pointer t.test.js::foo on a tree where TS-1 already carries TC-1-foo with the same acId, description, testPointer and status pending, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'TC-1-foo: unchanged (rcf/test-suites/ts-1.json)' and the file is not rewritten; given the same verb with --description "bar", it exits 3 naming the id and the differing field (description) and the file is not rewritten. Idempotency is id-carried: without --id, a derived-slug collision still refuses with exit 2 and the 'supply --slug explicitly' message.

AC-17302-12.description: [happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create cn --id CN-1 --path src/a.js --acs AC-1-1 on a tree where CN-1 already carries path src/a.js, implementsAcIds [AC-1-1], dependencies [], version 0.1.0 and status draft, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'CN-1: unchanged (rcf/code-nodes/cn-1.json)' and the file is not rewritten; given the same verb with --path src/b.js, it exits 3 naming the id and the differing field (path) and the file is not rewritten.

AC-17302-13.description: [happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create req --parent PRD-001 --id REQ-050 --title T --description D whose first run persisted a classifier-owned shapeClassification block, when the identical command is replayed, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'REQ-050: unchanged (rcf/requirements/req-050.json)' and the file is not rewritten: the replay compare ignores every writer- and classifier-owned field (createdAt, updatedAt, shapeClassification; one exported REPLAY_IGNORE_FIELDS list in src/core/store/writer.js); given the same verb with a different --description, it exits 3 naming description and the file is not rewritten.

AC-17302-14.description: [happy] (FBS-231 round 2) rcf define create ac keeps the criterion's scope field. A scope given in the --from-file body (a scopeTag value: library, runtime, deployed or unclassified) reaches the written criterion, as given, when, then and determinism do, whether the body carries the description or the CLI passes --description (CLI fields merged over the file, CLI wins); a same-id replay (--id, AC-17302-10) of a criterion that carries scope, with identical content, is unchanged (exit 0) and the file is not rewritten. rcf define create has no --scope flag: scope travels in --from-file. rcf define create us --from-file already keeps the scope of the criteria in its body.
AC-17302-14.given: a fixture project holding US-101, and a --from-file JSON body carrying scope beside given, when, then and (in the first form) description
AC-17302-14.when: rcf define create ac --parent US-101 --from-file <json> runs; rcf define create ac --parent US-101 --description <text> --from-file <json> runs; rcf define create ac --parent US-101 --id AC-101-1 --from-file <json> replays a criterion that already carries the same scope and content
AC-17302-14.then: rcf define read US-101 shows the written criterion carrying the scope from the file (runtime in the first form, library in the second), with description, given, when and then as given and the CLI description winning; the replay exits 0, stdout reads 'AC-101-1: unchanged (rcf/user-stories/us-101.json)' and the US file is byte-identical

AC-17401-2.description: Blocking stages in 0.29.0 (D1, D2, D4, D7, D8) report state 'passed' when every check ok is true, 'failing' when any check ok is false; warn-with-ack stages (D3, D5, D6) report 'passed' when every check ok is true, 'failing' when any check ok is false and the freeze record does NOT acknowledge that gate at the current tree hash, and 'acknowledged' when the freeze.gates[<gate>] entry names state 'acknowledged' and at.hash === currentTreeHash and any check ok is false.

AC-17401-3.description: notApplicable is decided per stage per proposal section 3.2: D2 notApplicable when no statement of a resolving kind (capability, constraint, entity, actor, externalSystem, surface) is in the delta AND no REQ, PRD or TAD is in scope; D3 notApplicable when no TAC and no shaped REQ (httpApi/persistence/auth) is in scope; D5 notApplicable when no REQ is in scope; D7 notApplicable when no open decisions exist AND the profile sets skipReviewFor: singleDocument AND the delta holds exactly one document; D4 and D6 use their own rules; D1 and D8 never notApplicable.

AC-17401-4.description: checkD4Stories enforces the D4 floors: every REQ in scope has a US (fail: 'no owning user story'), every US in scope has a testable AC ('missing testable AC'), a failure AC (parsed by the bracketed [failure] prefix on AC description) or a reasoned opt-out per class (manifest.baselineAcOptOuts[] entry with baselineKey 'defineD4:failure' and matching scope), a must-not AC (parsed by [must-not] prefix) or a reasoned opt-out per class (baselineKey 'defineD4:mustNot'), tacIds non-empty and every named tac resolving to a real TAC, and no AC description contains the scaffold TODO placeholder.

AC-17401-5.description: checkD3Shapes runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: every TAC in scope has at least one interface (fail: 'no interfaces authored'), and every interface's kind is in the closed vocabulary { recordShape, httpRoute, event, cliCommand, uiRoute, port, fileFormat, fixture, other } (fail: 'unknown interface kind <k>'). The template parser, entity-name join, ownerRef and path resolution are named seams (not called this slice) and D3 stays warn-with-ack.

AC-17401-6.description: checkD5Crosscut runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: TAD.securityArchitecture non-empty when the tree carries any REQ whose shapeClassification.shapes includes 'auth' or 'httpApi'; TAD.operationalConcerns non-empty when any AC description carries the '[deployed]' marker (a cheap presence signal proposal section 3.2 D5 lists as 'deployed-scope AC'); concern-ledger entries in scope disposed as 'applied' or 'waived' (no dangling 'open' concerns on REQs in scope). The full catalogue and per-pair enumeration are named seams for 0.30.

AC-17401-7.description: checkD6Consistency runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: validate is clean tree-wide (validateErrors is empty; the caller passes the walker + validator's error list), and probe-ledger holds zero 'open' probe entries. Contradiction-lite, unsatisfiable-lite, duplicates and orphan-interface scans, plus the probe runner, are named seams for 0.30.

AC-17401-8.description: checkD8Freeze enforces the tree-wide gate: every prior stage state (D1..D7 as computeReadiness composes them) is passed or acknowledged at the current hash; every AC id in the tree is bound by exactly one FBS (walker fbsByAcId map has length 1); the queue head (computeQueue.nextActionable) is actionable OR the queue is empty because every FBS is complete or verified (a fully built tree, emitted as freeze:queueEmptyAllBuilt in place of freeze:queueHead so consumers tell the two apart); validateErrors is empty. The stage is never notApplicable.

AC-17501-1.description: computeReadiness(tree, { freeze, ledgers, profile, testPointers }) returns the exact section 2.4 shape: tree { frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, buildAt, fbsTotal }, delta { changed, added, removed, briefSince, impacted, impactedFbs }, stages [{ stage, gate, state, checks }], nextAction { stage, check, ids, command } or null, coverage { tree, delta }, decisions [...open in #241 format], freezeable boolean. freezeable is true when every stage state is 'passed', 'acknowledged' or 'notApplicable'.

AC-17501-2.description: Fan-out is computed by calling computeImpact once per id in the union of changed and added; impacted is the union of every impact node id excluding the pivots; impactedFbs is the subset whose kind is 'fbs' and actionNeeded is 're-execute'. Gates run over scope = changed union added union impacted (with duplicates removed).

AC-17501-3.description: Coverage is tree-wide plus per REQ ancestor of the delta: coverage.tree is computeCoverage(tree, { testPointers, strict: true }) once over the whole tree; coverage.delta is an array with one CoverageResult per unique REQ id reachable by walking back from every delta id (changed union added) through parentByChild until the reqId is found, using scopeId per invocation. testPointers is the map the CLI produced with resolveTestPointers.

AC-17501-4.description: nextAction picks the first stage in D1..D8 order whose state is 'failing', then the first failing check in that stage's checks[] (or the check with the largest failing.length when tie); it names the stage id, the check name, the failing ids (deduped), and a command string like 'rcf define readiness --check <stage-short-name> after editing'. nextAction is null when every stage is passed / acknowledged / notApplicable.

AC-17501-5.description: rcf define readiness prints a text summary: the tree line ('Frozen at <shortHash> on <frozenAt>. N documents changed since, M impacted. Build at <fbsId> of <total>; K FBS impacted.' or 'Unfrozen. N documents; the whole tree is the delta.'), the next action line, a chip line 'D1:passed D2:failing D3:acknowledged D4:notApplicable ...', and the failing-items list per stage. --json emits the full computeReadiness object under `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\n`. --check <stage> (D1..D8 or short name brief|skeleton|shapes|stories|crosscut|consistency|decisions|freeze) prints only that stage and exits 0 when its state is 'passed' or 'acknowledged' or 'notApplicable', exit 4 on 'failing' for blocking stages (D1, D2, D4, D7, D8), exit 0 with a visible '[warn]' line on 'failing' for warn-with-ack stages (D3, D5, D6). The verb wraps its producer with runWithAdmissibilityGate and, on admissibility refusal, prints the refusal on stderr and exits 4.

AC-17501-6.description: loadAllLedgers({ projectRoot }) returns a LedgerBundle that OMITS a ledger key when the sidecar file does not exist (ENOENT), so computeDelta records no docHash for absent ledgers; the docstring on computeDelta (LedgerBundle typedef) and the loader implementation agree. A project that has authored a brief ledger and no others sees exactly one 'ledger:brief' entry in the delta docHashes; a project that has authored no ledgers sees zero 'ledger:*' entries.

AC-17601-1.description: [happy] rcf define freeze runs computeReadiness once over walkTree(projectRoot) plus loadFreezeRecord and loadAllLedgers. When result.freezeable is true, it writes rcf/define/freeze.json via saveFreezeRecord with these fields: frozenAt (ISO UTC now), treeHash (result.tree.currentTreeHash), docHashes (delta.js currentHashes over the live tree plus 'ledger:<name>' for each ledger present), briefStatements (the count of statements in the brief ledger, ledgers.brief.statements.length or 0), gates (one entry per stage-gate with { state, at: { hash, at, reason?, by? } | null, failing: [{ id, why }] } from the live readiness plus any --ack entries), counts { req, us, ac, acByClass: { happy, edge, failure, mustNot, nonFunctional, unclassified }, tac, interfaces: { <kind>: n, ... }, adr, fbs }, litmus { attestedAt, readers: 0 }, versions { rcfLite, ruleset, schemas } read from package.json, src/ruleset/ruleset.json and node_modules/@stravica-ai/rcf-schemas/package.json, note (--note argument or null), override (always null on a fresh freeze). The verb exits 0. Immediately after the write, calling computeDelta over the live tree + the new freeze reports every list empty (changed / added / removed / briefSince).

AC-17601-2.description: [failure] When result.freezeable is false and no --ack argument covers the failing stage, the verb exits 4 without writing the freeze record. It prints the failing gates (one per line: '<stage> (<gate>): failing (<first check name>); failing ids: <id1>, <id2>, ...' capped at 20 ids per gate) to stderr, followed by the exact rcf define readiness --check <shortName> command that will re-print the same block for each failing stage. The file at rcf/define/freeze.json is not created or modified (a pre-existing file is byte-identical after the refusal).

AC-17601-3.description: [failure] --ack <gate> --reason <text> is accepted only for the three warn-with-ack gates: define.shapes / D3 / shapes, define.crosscut / D5 / crosscut, define.consistency / D6 / consistency (the same STAGE_ALIASES readiness accepts). --ack on any other gate name is a usage refusal (exit 2) with a stderr message naming the accepted set. --ack without a matching --reason argument is a usage refusal (exit 2). Multiple --ack / --reason pairs may be passed together (parseArgs multiple: true) as long as the count matches; a mismatch is a usage refusal. An acked gate lands in the written freeze.gates entry as { state: 'acknowledged', at: { hash: <currentTreeHash>, at: <frozenAt>, reason: <text>, by: <freezerId or null> }, failing: [<id>, ...] } and its acknowledgement carries into the next computeReadiness run (which reports the stage state as 'acknowledged').

AC-17601-4.description: [happy] The stdout summary derived from the delta BEFORE the freeze matches proposal section 2.5: 'frozen at <shortHash>: <n> REQ, <n> stories, <n> criteria, <n> interfaces added; <ids> amended; <impactedFbs> re-execute.' Counts of added come from delta.added grouped by tree.kindById; amended is delta.changed (US ids in the amended list per the proposal's example wording); impactedFbs is delta.impactedFbs. On the first freeze (freeze record absent before the run), the summary is 'first freeze at <shortHash>: <req> REQ, <us> stories, <ac> criteria, <interfaces> interfaces, <tac> TAC, <adr> ADR, <fbs> FBS.' --json emits { record, summary, delta } where record is the just-written freeze record body and delta is the pre-freeze DeltaResult.

AC-17601-5.description: [happy] --status prints the current record and the live delta summary, exit 0. Text: 'Frozen at <short> on <frozenAt>. Note: <note|(none)>. Counts: <req> REQ / <us> US / <ac> AC / <tac> TAC / <adr> ADR / <fbs> FBS. Acknowledged: <gate1> ("<reason>"); <gate2> ...(none). Litmus: attestedAt [<D3>, <D6>], readers <n>. Versions: rcfLite <v> / ruleset <v> / schemas <v>. Override: <null|<reason by at>>.' followed by the live delta summary line: '<changed> changed, <added> added, <removed> removed, <impacted> impacted, <impactedFbs> FBS re-execute.' --status --json emits { record: <freeze body>, delta: <computeDelta output> }. --status when no record exists prints 'never frozen' and exits 0 (--json: { record: null, delta: <computeDelta output over unfrozen tree> }). --status never runs the gates and never writes anything.

AC-17601-6.description: [happy] The freeze producer is wrapped with runWithAdmissibilityGate the same way readiness is (ADR-4124 carrying ADR-4123): the wrap runs first so the ruleset toolScope guard is honoured, and on a refused-admissibility verdict the CLI prints the refusal envelope to stderr as a [warn] line and the freeze compute still runs and writes if freezeable. The verb never exits 4 solely because of a refused-admissibility verdict.

AC-17601-7.description: [must-not] src/define/freeze-record.js is updated so validateFreezeRecord REQUIRES the override key (nullable): a body without override throws FreezeRecordError with field 'override'. loadFreezeRecord tolerates older records that lack the key by defaulting to null (never fails on ENOKEY). saveFreezeRecord validates first and refuses to write a body that omits override. Every existing test fixture that omits override still loads (either the loader default fills it in, or a targeted fixture update writes override: null; no legacy fixture becomes unreadable).

AC-17601-8.description: [non-functional] The src/cli/readiness.js stage header line no longer contains a double-dash: it uses a colon between the stage id and the state label ('D1 (define.brief): failing'). Any golden fixture that captured the old header text is updated. `grep -R ' -- ' src/ test/ CHANGELOG.md` returns no matches under text this slice added or edited (the grep is scoped to added lines; unrelated pre-existing occurrences elsewhere in the tree stay out of scope of the AC).
