AC-18801-1.description: [happy] given a coreEntities entry whose description starts with [draft], when D3 runs, then shapes:draftSettled fails TAD.entity:<name>.

AC-18801-2.description: [happy] given a TAC whose purpose starts with [draft], when D3 runs, then shapes:draftSettled fails <tacId> and shapes:tacHasInterface treats the TAC as present.

AC-18801-3.description: [happy] given the three marker homes cleared, when D3 runs, then shapes:draftSettled passes.

AC-18801-4.description: [failure] given a [draft] recordShape without fields:, when D3 runs, then shapes:templateMarkers fails it exactly as a settled one.

AC-18801-5.description: [must-not] given any [draft] content, when readiness runs, then no productOwner check reads it.

AC-18901-1.description: [happy] Given an intake run carrying --ui with a value from [none | light | central], when intake writes the intakeClassification, then rcf/discovery/journey.json exists with JourneyRecord.ui equal to the declared value, JourneyRecord.declaredVia equal to "intake" and JourneyRecord.declaredAt equal to the run time.

AC-18901-2.description: [happy] Given a tree with or without an existing journey.json, when the operator runs the journey declare verb with --ui and a value from [none | light | central], then journey.json exists with JourneyRecord.ui equal to the value and JourneyRecord.declaredVia equal to "declare", --as-built sets JourneyRecord.asBuilt true and its absence leaves the field as it was (false on a record intake or init wrote), and lowering the value (central to light, or light or central to none) without --reason is refused with exit 2 naming the flag while the same call with --reason records the reason on the record.

AC-18901-3.description: [happy] Given an interactive intake run with no --ui flag, when intake reaches the declaration, then it prints the shared matcher's UI signals over the artefact text (an empty list when none match) and the proposed value (none when no signal matched), asks for the declaration, and the value written is the one the operator typed, never the proposal.

AC-18901-4.description: [failure] Given a non-interactive intake run through --input with no ui field, when it runs, with or without UI signals in the artefact text, then intake exits 2 naming the ui field and writes neither the intakeClassification nor journey.json, so no intake on this version completes without a declaration.

AC-18901-5.description: [edge] Given a tree with no rcf/discovery/journey.json, when readJourneyRecord reads it, then it returns null (the grandfathered state every later reader folds to notApplicable), and rcf discover intake --dry-run and rcf discover journey declare --dry-run on that tree print the record they would write and leave rcf/discovery/ absent.

AC-18901-6.description: [edge] Given rcf init on this version, when the tree is created, then rcf/discovery/journey.json is written with JourneyRecord.ui null, JourneyRecord.declaredVia "init" and JourneyRecord.asBuilt false, and readJourneyRecord returns that record rather than null, so a new project is never read as a grandfathered tree.

AC-18901-7.description: [must-not] Given a tree with no journey.json, when rcf doctor runs with or without --fix, then the missing declaration appears under notices as advice and never under drift, the exit code is unchanged by it, and --fix never writes the record.

AC-18902-1.description: [happy] Given a journey source file in the line grammar, when the journey add verb runs with --from, then journey.json gains one Journey whose JourneyStep entries carry JNY-nnn-nnn ids in file order, each step kind from [entry | step | exit | interruption], each step screen resolved by slug to a Screen minted as SCR-nnn on first sight, and Journey.source equal to the file path.

AC-18902-2.description: [happy] Given a journey already minted, when its source is edited and the journey add verb runs again with --from, then every step whose slug is unchanged keeps its JourneyStep.id, a new slug mints the next number, and a removed slug's number is never reused by a later mint.

AC-18902-3.description: [happy] Given a journey-map document in the prose shape (an H2 heading per step, a Screen: wf-NN-slug line and zero or more Goes to: wf-NN-slug lines), when the journey import verb runs with --from, then the record minted is the one the line grammar would produce for the same journey, with the first heading as the entry, a heading with no Goes to line as an exit, and each wf-NN-slug resolved to a Screen whose Screen.wireframe is the file of the same stem beside the source when it exists.

AC-18902-4.description: [happy] Given a minted record, when the journey show verb runs, then it prints each journey's steps in order with id, kind, screen slug, label, next and returnsTo, the interruption answers and the review state, and with --json emits the JourneyRecord verbatim.

AC-18902-5.description: [failure] Given a source line outside the grammar (a missing kind, a missing @screen-slug, or an interruption with no returns target), when the journey add verb runs with --from, then it exits 3 naming the file, the line number and the rule, and journey.json is not written.

AC-18902-6.description: [edge] Given --dry-run on the journey add or import verb, when it runs, then the planned mints are printed, the same local schema pass the write path runs is applied, and journey.json is byte-identical before and after.

AC-18902-7.description: [must-not] Given any journey verb, when it writes journey.json, then it never accepts a hand-supplied JNY or SCR id, never records a Figma or Confluence link as Screen.wireframe, and the walker's document count is unchanged by the file (rcf/discovery/ is invisible to the loader).

AC-18903-1.description: [happy] Given a declared light or central product with a journey, when the journey check verb runs, then it evaluates discovery:journeyPresent (at least one journey with an entry and an exit), discovery:stepsNameScreens (every JourneyStep.screenId resolves), discovery:reachable (every step reachable from an entry and every non-exit step with a next or a returnsTo) and discovery:interruptions, prints one line per check, and exits 0 when every check passes.

AC-18903-2.description: [happy] Given the interruption catalogue [lostEmail | closedTab | deadBattery | expiredLink | switchedDevice | lostSignal], when discovery:interruptions evaluates a journey, then each catalogue entry is either covered by a step of that journey, of any kind, or ruled out as notApplicable with a reason of at least 20 characters, and an entry that is neither fails the check with an id naming the journey and the entry.

AC-18903-3.description: [happy] Given a central product, when discovery:wireframePerStep evaluates, then it fails for every step whose Screen.wireframe is null or does not resolve on disk, and given a light product the same check reports notApplicable and never fails for a missing wireframe.

AC-18903-4.description: [happy] Given a wireframe file, when the check reads it, then a .md file is accepted as-is, an .html file is accepted when no href, src or srcset attribute value and no CSS url() or @import target (in a style element or a style attribute) starts http:, https: or //, a .png file is accepted only when JourneyRecord.asBuilt is true, and the file's bytes are hashed with sha256 without any inspection of its headings or sections.

AC-18903-5.description: [failure] Given an .html wireframe carrying an external stylesheet, script, image or font URL through any of href, src, srcset, CSS url() or @import, when the journey check verb runs, then discovery:wireframeSelfContained fails naming the file and the first offending URL and the verb exits 4.

AC-18903-6.description: [edge] Given a journey with a non-exit step that has no next and no returnsTo, when discovery:reachable evaluates, then it fails naming that step as a dead end, distinct from the why it gives a step no entry reaches.

AC-18903-7.description: [must-not] Given a declared none product or a tree with no declared journey record (absent file or ui null), when the journey check verb runs, then it reports notApplicable with the reason, reads no wireframe file, and exits 0.

AC-18903-8.description: [failure] Given a Screen.wireframe whose extension is outside .md, .html and .png, or a .png on a record whose JourneyRecord.asBuilt is false, when the journey check verb runs, then discovery:wireframeFormat fails naming the file and the rule it breaks and the verb exits 4, on a light product as on a central one.

AC-18904-1.description: [happy] Given a journey that passes every structural check, when the journey review verb runs with --by and a name, then ReviewStamp.state equals "reviewed", ReviewStamp.by equals the name, ReviewStamp.at carries the time and the discoveryHash of the record, and ReviewStamp.wireframeHashes carries one sha256 per screen with a wireframe.

AC-18904-2.description: [happy] Given a reviewed record, when discovery:reviewed evaluates with the record and every wireframe file unchanged, then it passes, and the review verb that produced the stamp printed the one-line summary (journeys, steps, screens, interruptions mapped) before writing.

AC-18904-3.description: [failure] Given a journey that fails any structural check, when the journey review verb runs, then it exits 4 printing the failing checks and writes no ReviewStamp.

AC-18904-4.description: [edge] Given a reviewed record, when a wireframe file's bytes change or a journey source is re-minted, then discovery:reviewed fails as stale with a why naming the changed screens or journey, and a second review at the new hash makes it pass again.

AC-18904-5.description: [must-not] Given the managed agent-instructions block, when rcf init or rcf doctor --fix writes it, then it carries the rule that the harness never runs the journey review verb on its own beside the ADR-4132 prototype rule, and no verb other than journey review ever writes ReviewStamp.

AC-18905-1.description: [happy] Given readiness computes, when the stages are listed, then D0 (gate define.discovery, short name discovery) precedes D1 in STAGE_ORDER, its policy is blocking, it is absent from WARN_WITH_ACK, every discovery:* check carries the productOwner persona, and rcf define readiness --check discovery exits 4 when D0 fails and 0 when it passes or is notApplicable.

AC-18905-2.description: [happy] Given a declared central product, when D0 evaluates, then it runs discovery:declared, discovery:journeyPresent, discovery:stepsNameScreens, discovery:reachable, discovery:interruptions, discovery:wireframePerStep, discovery:wireframeFormat, discovery:wireframeSelfContained and discovery:reviewed, and given a declared light product the same set runs with discovery:wireframePerStep and discovery:reviewed notApplicable, so a light product is never refused for a missing wireframe or a missing review.

AC-18905-3.description: [edge] Given a declared none product or a tree with no journey.json, when D0 evaluates, then it reports notApplicable with the reason "product declared not UI-bearing" or "no discovery declaration (existing tree)", journey.json is the only file under rcf/discovery/ read, and the door check passes without reading any other file.

AC-18905-4.description: [failure] Given a declared light or central product whose D0 fails, when rcf define ledger brief add, rcf define create or rcf define blueprint add runs, then it exits 4 before any write, the message begins "[error] refused define:" and names the declared value, the failing check, the failing ids and the readiness check to run, and the tree is byte-identical before and after.

AC-18905-5.description: [happy] Given a central product reviewed at the current hash, or a light product whose journey answers the catalogue whether or not it has been reviewed, when rcf define ledger brief add, rcf define create or rcf define blueprint add runs, then the door check passes and the write lands as it did before this requirement.

AC-18905-6.description: [must-not] Given D0 failing, when rcf define readiness --ack discovery or rcf define freeze runs, then no acknowledgement path exists for D0: --ack discovery exits 2 as not ackable and freeze refuses through its failing block naming D0.

AC-18905-7.description: [must-not] Given a product whose D0 fails, when rcf define update, delete, link, unlink, design, standards, the decisions, concerns or probes ledgers, readiness or questions run, then they are not gated and complete as they did before this requirement.

AC-18905-8.description: [happy] Given rcf define questions --persona productOwner on a failing D0, when it runs, then the D0 items come first, each with a plain question template and a write-back naming the journey verb that resolves it, and a none product or a grandfathered tree contributes no D0 question.

AC-18905-9.description: [failure] Given a record whose JourneyRecord.ui is null (the record rcf init writes), when D0 evaluates, then discovery:declared fails with a why naming the declare verb and the three values, D0 is failing, and the door check refuses as it does for any failing D0 until a declaration is made.

AC-18906-1.description: [happy] Given an FBS whose journeyStepIds all resolve to steps in journey.json, when rcf define validate and rcf build bundle run, then validate reports no finding for it and the bundle prints each bound step with its id, label, screen slug and Screen.wireframe path so the executor sees the map.

AC-18906-2.description: [happy] Given a light or central product, when rcf build queue runs, then its markdown and JSON output carry a journeySteps block with one StepState per step whose StepState.state is unbound when no FBS names the step and otherwise the least advanced bound executionStatus mapped as [notStarted to queued | inProgress to inProgress | complete to built | verified to verified], with StepState.fbsIds listing the build specs that name it, and the journey show verb prints the same state beside each step.

AC-18906-3.description: [happy] Given rcf build review on a light or central product, when it runs, then it emits one finding of kind journeyStub per step in state unbound and one per FBS with uiBearing true and no journeyStepIds, each with detail starting "journeyStub:" and anchorId the step id or the FBS id, and the exit code is unchanged by these findings.

AC-18906-4.description: [failure] Given an FBS whose journeyStepIds names an id that resolves to no step (a retired number or a typo), when rcf define validate runs, then it reports a brokenReference finding naming the FBS id and the unresolved id, and the journey show verb lists that FBS under a broken-binding line.

AC-18906-5.description: [edge] Given a step bound to two build specs with executionStatus complete and inProgress, when the state derives, then StepState.state is inProgress, and the same step with complete and verified derives built.

AC-18906-6.description: [must-not] Given journeyStepIds on any FBS, when rcf audit coverage, rcf audit trace or rcf audit impact run, then no journey or step id appears as a node or an edge in their output and the FBS designStage.journeys[] is unchanged by the binding.

AC-19001-1.description: [happy] Given a git checkout at head H and an FBS with bound ACs, when rcf verify run --url <preview-url> --fbs <fbs-id> --mode deterministic --hand verifier --verifier-id <id> runs, then rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/<first 12 of H>.json exists and validates as VerifyReport v1 with headSha H, target.kind "url", target.url the given URL, hand "verifier", verifierId the given id, mode, startedAt, finishedAt, rcfLiteVersion, verdict and one perAc row per bound AC, and stdout ends with "verify report: <path> <verdict> <verified>/<total>".

AC-19001-2.description: [failure] Given a working tree with uncommitted changes outside rcf/verify-reports/, when rcf verify run --hand verifier --fbs <fbs-id> runs, then it refuses with exit 4 and stderr "verify report refused: working tree is dirty; the report must name a committed head", and writes no report.

AC-19001-3.description: [failure] Given --hand with a value outside [test-author | builder | reviewer | verifier | stage-keeper], or --fbs absent while --hand is given, when rcf verify run is invoked, then it exits 2 naming the flag and writes no report.

AC-19001-4.description: [happy] Given a version-host target (a packed or published package rather than a web address), when rcf verify run --package <name@version|tarball> --fbs <fbs-id> --hand verifier runs, then the report carries target.kind "package" and target.packageRef and target.url is absent, so a CLI product verifies against its version host.

AC-19001-5.description: [happy] Given a committed report under rcf/verify-reports/, when rcf define validate and the tree walker run, then neither treats the directory as chain documents (validate exit 0, no unknown-document error).

AC-19001-6.description: [must-not] rcf verify run --hand verifier never writes outside rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/: after a run, git status lists no change under src/, test/ or any chain document directory, and an existing report for the same head is never overwritten (a second run exits 4 with "verify report exists for head <sha7>; pass --replace \"<reason>\"").

AC-19001-7.description: [failure] rcf verify run --out takes a file path. Given --out naming an existing directory (with or without a trailing path separator) on a --url run without --hand, when rcf verify run is invoked, then it exits 2 before any request reaches the target, stderr carries "--out must be a file path, not a directory" (as "[error] usage --out must be a file path, not a directory: <value>"), and nothing is written inside the directory; rcf verify run --help describes --out as a file path and says a directory is refused (exit 2). A --out naming a file path still writes the report there.

AC-19002-1.description: [happy] Given an FBS at complete, HEAD containing the report head, every bound AC with a Code Node, and a valid VerifyReport with hand "verifier", verdict PASS with ship authority and finishedAt within 7 days, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then executionStatus becomes verified, stdout carries "finalise: <fbs-id> verified from <report path> (head <sha7>, ci <ref>)", it exits 0, and no child process other than git is spawned.

AC-19002-2.description: [failure] Given no report under rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/ (and no --report), when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: no Test-stage verify report for <fbs-id>; the verifier runs rcf verify run --fbs <fbs-id> --hand verifier before merge" and the FBS stays complete.

AC-19002-3.description: [failure] Given a report whose headSha is neither an ancestor of HEAD nor tree-equal to a commit HEAD contains, when Finalise runs, then it exits 4 with "finalise refused: report head <sha7> is not contained in HEAD <sha7>; re-verify this head"; a finishedAt older than --max-report-age (default 7 days) exits 4 with "finalise refused: report is <n> days old".

AC-19002-4.description: [failure] Given a report whose hand is not "verifier", or whose verifierId equals the Hand-Id trailer of any Hand: builder commit between the merge-base and HEAD, when Finalise runs, then it exits 4 with "finalise refused: report hand <hand>/<id> is not separate from the builder" and the FBS is unchanged.

AC-19002-5.description: [failure] Given --ci-run absent, the FBS not at complete, or a bound AC without a Code Node, when Finalise runs, then it exits 4 ("ci evidence missing: pass --ci-run <ref>"), 4 (the existing not-complete message) and 3 ("missing Code Nodes: <ac-ids>") respectively; a report that fails VerifyReport v1 validation exits 3 naming the field.

AC-19002-6.description: [failure] Given a valid report whose perAc rows carry any verdict from [MOCK-ONLY-DECLARED | EVAL-MISSING | EVAL-BELOW-THRESHOLD | UI-BASELINE-UNMET | BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING | SCOPE-MISMATCH], or whose verdict is not PASS or verdictAuthority is not ship, when Finalise runs, then it refuses exit 4 with the same message shapes 0.20.0 and 0.28.0 defined, read from the ingested report, and the FBS stays complete.

AC-19002-7.description: [failure] Given the retired flags, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --mode <any> or --url <url> runs, then it exits 2 with "finalise no longer runs verify; run rcf verify run --fbs <fbs-id> --hand verifier at the Test stage" and spawns nothing.

AC-19002-8.description: [must-not] rcf build finalise never spawns rcf verify run, the verifier package or the agent CLI, and on every refusal leaves rcf/fbs/<fbs-id>.json byte-identical to its state before the run.

AC-19003-1.description: [failure] Given rcf/define/backstop.json with fromBuildOrder N and an FBS with buildOrder >= N at complete, when rcf build bundle --next runs, then it exits 4 with "backstop: <k> merged spec(s) complete and not verified: <ids>; run rcf build finalise <id> or pass --allow-unverified \"<reason>\"" and emits no bundle.

AC-19003-2.description: [happy] Given the same tree, when rcf build bundle --next --allow-unverified "hotfix while FBS-xxx re-verifies" runs, then the bundle is emitted, backstop.overrides in rcf/define/backstop.json gains { reason, by, at, unverifiedFbsIds } and stdout carries "backstop overridden: <reason>"; an empty reason exits 2.

AC-19003-3.description: [edge] Given a tree with no rcf/define/backstop.json, or one whose complete FBS all have buildOrder below fromBuildOrder, when rcf build bundle --next runs, then the backstop does not refuse and the bundle behaves as before.

AC-19003-4.description: [happy] Given a tree without a backstop record, when rcf build backstop adopt --from FBS-218 runs, then rcf/define/backstop.json holds { fromBuildOrder: 218, adoptedAt, adoptedBy } and the command exits 0; an unknown FBS id exits 3 and a missing --from exits 2.

AC-19003-5.description: [must-not] rcf build bundle --next never emits a bundle while the backstop refuses unless --allow-unverified carries a non-empty reason, and the override never changes any FBS executionStatus.

AC-19004-1.description: [happy] When rcf guidance build-cycle runs, then the Test stage text names the verifier hand, rcf verify run --fbs <fbs-id> --hand verifier against the preview or version host, the committed report under rcf/verify-reports/ and the merge gate (Review MERGE plus Test PASS); the Finalise stage text names CI green, merge, rcf build mark <fbs-id> complete and rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> ingesting the report; and the output contains neither "--url <deploy-url>" on the finalise line nor "post-merge verify run".

AC-19004-2.description: [happy] When rcf guidance build-cycle runs, then the Define stage text names the test-author hand writing AC-based and E2E tests and TS/TC bindings, the Build stage names the builder writing production code, Code Nodes and code-hygiene unit tests only, and every stage names its Hand: trailer value.

AC-19004-3.description: [happy] When rcf build bundle --next --format md emits a bundle, then its closing runbook lists the five stages with their hands, the rcf verify run Test-stage command with --hand verifier, rcf audit separation, and the rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> line, and no finalise line carries --mode or --url.

AC-19004-4.description: [happy] When rcf guidance managed/agent-instructions-block runs after the release, then the block states that verified is written only by rcf build finalise from a Test-stage report, the release notes carry a non-null minAgentAction telling agents to refresh the block with rcf doctor, and rcf doctor reports the old block as drifted.

AC-19004-5.description: [happy] When the README at the repository root and every guidance topic printed by rcf guidance are searched for the stage chain, then the fifth verb reads audit (define, build, verify, release, audit) and attest appears nowhere as a verb or stage name; the unrelated AC attestation vocabulary and the --litmus-attested flag stay as they are.

AC-19004-6.description: [failure] Given a project whose CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md carries the pre-change managed block, when rcf doctor runs with the new release, then it reports the managed block as drifted, names rcf doctor --fix as the refresh command and does not exit 0.

AC-19004-7.description: [must-not] no guidance topic printed by rcf guidance and no bundle runbook from rcf build bundle --next tells a hand to run rcf build finalise with --mode or --url, or to run verification after merge.

AC-19005-1.description: [happy] Given a git working tree on a branch other than main or master whose HEAD contains the report head, the FBS at complete with a Code Node on every bound AC, and a committed valid VerifyReport with hand "verifier" and verdict PASS with ship authority, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs with no other flag, then it exits 0, executionStatus becomes verified on that branch, stdout carries "finalise: <fbs-id> verified from <report path> (head <sha7>, ci <ref>)", stderr carries no "not a default trunk" refusal, no output names claim C-26, and no child process other than git is spawned.

AC-19005-10.description: [happy] When rcf build finalise --help, rcf build --help, rcf guidance build-cycle, rcf guidance build-cycle-playbook (sections 6 and 7 together), the managed block rcf init writes into CLAUDE.md and the rcf build bundle --next --format md runbook (its Stage 5 section) are read, then each contains "on the PR branch before the merge", the word "loopback", and "served sha" or "servedSha"; and none of rcf build finalise --help, rcf build --help, rcf guidance build-cycle, the whole rcf guidance build-cycle-playbook, the managed block or the whole bundle runbook contains "the CI run that passed on the merged head", a mark-complete step after the merge ("mark" then "complete" then "after merge" or "after the merge" within one sentence), "After the merge" followed by an rcf build mark or rcf build finalise command, or "marking complete before the merge" or "marking complete pre-merge".

AC-19005-2.description: [happy] Given a committed VerifyReport whose target is loopback (localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0) and names target.engine (non-empty text), target.port (an integer 1 to 65535) and target.servedSha equal to its headSha, with hand "verifier" and verdict PASS with ship authority, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then it exits 0, executionStatus becomes verified, stdout carries the verified-from line and no output carries "is loopback".

AC-19005-3.description: [failure] Given a committed VerifyReport whose target is loopback and lacks target.engine, target.port or target.servedSha, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: loopback report target <url> names no target.<field>" naming the first missing field in the order engine, port, servedSha, and rcf/fbs/<fbs-id>.json is byte-identical to its state before the run.

AC-19005-4.description: [failure] Given a committed loopback VerifyReport naming target.engine and target.port whose target.servedSha is not equal to its headSha, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: report target.servedSha <served sha7> is not the report head <head sha7>" and rcf/fbs/<fbs-id>.json is byte-identical to its state before the run.

AC-19005-5.description: [happy] Given a clean working tree at a committed HEAD and a server on a loopback --url, when rcf verify run --url <loopback-url> --fbs <fbs-id> --mode deterministic --hand verifier --verifier-id <id> --engine <name> --served-sha <sha> runs with <sha> the full sha of the committed HEAD, then the report it writes under rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/<head12>.json records target { kind "url", url, engine <name>, port <the URL's port as an integer, or 80 / 443 by scheme when the URL names none>, servedSha <sha> }. A --served-sha that is not the full sha of the committed HEAD exits 4 with stderr "verify report refused: --served-sha <value> is not the committed HEAD <sha7>"; a loopback --url with --hand and no --engine exits 2 with stderr "[error] usage --engine <name> is required with --hand and a loopback --url"; with --engine and no --served-sha it exits 2 with stderr "[error] usage --served-sha <sha> is required with --hand and a loopback --url". Whenever the target is not a --url (a directory, a tarball, or a name@version: --artefact <tgz>, or --package <dir | tarball | name@version> with no --url), --engine exits 2 with stderr "[error] usage --engine applies only to a --url target; a non-URL target (directory, tarball or name@version) has no served URL" and --served-sha exits 2 with stderr "[error] usage --served-sha applies only to a --url target; a non-URL target (directory, tarball or name@version) has no served URL", with or without --hand, before any pack, install or engine call. Every refusal writes no report and sends no probe request.

AC-19005-6.description: [failure] Given the report Finalise selects (the newest under rcf/verify-reports/<fbs-id>/, or --report) present on disk but not committed in HEAD, when rcf build finalise <fbs-id> --ci-run <ref> runs, then it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: verify report <path> is not committed at HEAD"; given it is committed but its bytes on disk differ from its bytes at HEAD, it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: verify report <path> differs from its committed bytes at HEAD"; given --report names a path that does not resolve to a file under the project root, it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: verify report <path> is outside the project root" before the file is read; given the report path, or any component of it below the repo root, is a symbolic link (checked with lstat, never followed), it exits 4 with stderr "finalise refused: verify report <path> is read through a symlink at <link>", <link> the repo-relative path of the first such component, so the committed-and-clean check and the read run on the real file only; <path> is the repo-relative report path, and rcf/fbs/<fbs-id>.json is byte-identical to its state before the run in every case.

AC-2201-1.description: The blueprint loader accepts an optional capabilities[] top-level field on blueprint.json: when present it must be a non-empty array of lower camelCase strings on ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$, and a malformed value refuses with a validation rcfError naming the field. AC-2201-2.description: The blueprint loader accepts an optional elicits[] top-level field: when present it must be a non-empty array of {id (kebab slug), prompt (non-empty operator-facing string, no em-dashes, no emojis), kind (one of enum, string, boolean), default (matching kind), options (required when kind=enum), when (optional predicate object)} entries; malformed shapes refuse with a validation rcfError naming the entry.
